tickets.title: MCP hot reload waits for idle instead of holding new calls behind in-flight ones
tickets.live_try: during a hud_land of a MyHUD job (which rebuilds dist), call hud_tickets guide and hud_peek from the main session: both return within a second
tickets.what: Diagnosis job j728520f939adb5de (read its full report). Today packages/hud-mcp/bin/hud-mcp.mjs:34-40,69-76 starts a reload as soon as the build stamp changes and drains ALL outstanding calls before handing off; new stdin lines wait for the handoff, so a ticket edit waiting minutes on the main-checkout lease holds unrelated calls (guide, peek, even ping) for minutes (reproduced 121 s). Change: defer starting the reload until no call is in flight; keep dispatching new calls to the current generation meanwhile; reload on the next idle moment. Never migrate or replay a mutation. Adapt the existing 'rebuild drains overlapping' test in tests/unit/thin-mcp-reload.test.mjs: a changed stamp with one long call in flight leaves new guide/peek/ping answering in milliseconds, no call is replayed, the reload happens once idle and state is preserved.

acceptance.text: With a stamp change and a long in-flight call, new unrelated calls answer within 50 ms on the old generation (test)
No call is replayed; the reload happens at the first idle moment and preserves state (test)
Existing reload tests pass; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md reload note updated

tickets.title: Ticket edits under a held land lease return a queued receipt within 2 s and commit in order later
tickets.live_try: while a hud_land runs, call hud_tickets add for a scratch feature in a temp project: it returns queued within 2 s; after the land finishes the ticket file and commit appear and the receipt shows its number
tickets.what: Diagnosis job j728520f939adb5de, proposal 2. Today src/mcp/ticket-commits.ts:16-32 waits for the main-checkout lease (held by land through gate, publish and cleanup, src/mcp/land-runner.ts:532-593) before planning or writing, so hud_tickets add/update block for minutes (647 s observed). Keep the synchronous fast path when the lease is free (unchanged reply). When the lease is held: admit the edit to an ordered, private, bounded durable queue under $HUD_HOME and return within 2 s `state: queued` with a receipt id (no assigned paths or per-item outcomes yet; say so in the reply). Admission must not wait behind another edit's lease wait. After the lease is granted, revalidate against the current checkout, apply with the existing path-only commit and hand-edit protections, and record the outcome on the receipt; recovery after an MCP restart applies each receipt at most once (no duplicate adds). Read the outcome with hud_read({job: <receipt>}) or a hud_tickets op the main session already uses, whichever adds less surface; a finished receipt also reaches the caller like other notices. Keep chores/02: edits never write into the main checkout while a land holds it. Update docs/reference.md (hud_tickets) and the tool description in as few words as the schema budget allows.

acceptance.text: Lease free: add/update reply as today, under 2 s (test)
Lease held: reply `queued` with a receipt in under 2 s; a second edit is admitted without waiting behind the first (test)
After the lease is released, queued edits apply in admission order with path-only commits; receipt shows assigned numbers/paths or the error (test)
MCP restart with pending receipts applies each once, no duplicates (test)
docs/reference.md and tool description updated

tickets.title: A queued ticket edit always reaches a terminal outcome even when its drain helper fails
tickets.live_try: While a hud_land of a MyHUD job runs, call hud_tickets add for a scratch feature in a temp project and kill the spawned `workflow-runner --ticket-edits` helper; after the land finishes, without another submission, hud_read on the receipt shows completed (ticket file and commit present) or failed with a reason, never stuck queued
tickets.what: Repair from milestone review jd2fc9755a1a3a2b6 (finding 'accepted edit can remain queued indefinitely'). Today src/mcp/ticket-edit-queue.ts:29-40 `wake()` drops spawn errors and ignores an early helper exit. The detached runner can fail its dist import/lock (packages/hud-mcp/bin/workflow-runner.mjs:8-10), for example during the rebuild of the very land that caused the queueing. `settle()` can also throw out of `drainTicketEdits` when `takeLease` itself errors. Either way the receipt stays queued/active and nothing re-drives it: `hud_read` only reads the row (ticket-edit-queue.ts:42-46), and a hot swap skips `resumeTicketEdits` (src/mcp/mcp/server.ts:293-301). Only another submission or a cold MCP restart recovers it. Fix: the MCP that admitted (or still holds) pending receipts re-drives them on a bounded trigger, so no caller action is needed. Use the simplest of these: a recovery check when the drain mutex is free and the receipt is still active, run from the existing notice/idle path or a bounded timer, and/or on hot-swap start. When the helper exits without settling, re-wake it a bounded number of times. Past that bound, record a definite `failed` with the launch error. Never replay a receipt that is already `applying`; the existing commit-marker check still decides it. Also, while there, avoid re-parsing every retained terminal receipt on each admission and each drained item when only active ids are needed (optional simplification from the same review), but only if that stays small.

acceptance.text: The first helper launch fails (or the helper exits before settling); after the lease is released, the receipt reaches completed or failed without another submission or a cold MCP restart (test)
An `applying` receipt is never applied twice by the re-drive; the commit-marker check decides it (test)
Re-wake attempts are bounded; past the bound the receipt is `failed` with the reason, and the caller gets the usual completion notice (test)
Existing thin-mcp-ticket-commits tests still pass

tickets.title: A ticket edit queued by a lead still reaches a terminal outcome after the lead's MCP swaps or exits
tickets.live_try: While a hud_land of a MyHUD job runs, have a lead in a queue run call hud_tickets add for a scratch feature in a temp project (gets `state: queued`), let the lead report and close, then kill the spawned `workflow-runner --ticket-edits` helper; with no main MCP restart and no further submission, hud_read on the receipt shows completed (ticket file and commit present) or failed with a reason, never stuck queued
tickets.what: Repair from milestone review j2814424269891a3c (major finding). Leads may call the main hud_tickets handler (src/mcp/mcp/server.ts:192-200), and a lead's add/update admits a queued receipt and starts its supervisor (src/mcp/ticket-edit-queue.ts submitTicketEdit -> wake). But a lead's MCP has HUD_JOB_DIR set, so `worker` is truthy. Neither cold start (server.ts:297-300) nor hot swap (server.ts:326) calls resumeTicketEdits for it, and stop() aborts the supervisor unconditionally. A lead session also closes right after hud_report, which ends its supervisor. If the detached `workflow-runner --ticket-edits` helper then fails, which is the case ticket 03 covers, the receipt stays `queued` until some main MCP starts or reloads. Unattended runs need not have a main session open. This happens in practice: lead j66891978899adb94 reported with receipt te…2d2 still queued behind consecutive lands. Fix with the simplest of these: (a) give resume (cold start and hot swap) the same eligibility as admission (main or lead); and (b) so the receipt survives the lead closing, have the long-lived process that hosts the lead step (the queue workflow runner, src/mcp/workflow-runner.ts) re-drive active receipts for its project with the existing resumeTicketEdits/wake supervisor while the run is alive, then stop it when the run ends. Reuse the existing bounded wake, its attempt budget, and the commit-marker check. Add no second drainer and no new receipt API. Never replay an `applying` receipt.

acceptance.text: A lead MCP that admitted a queued receipt resumes its supervision after a hot swap (and on cold start), using the same eligibility as admission (test)
With no main MCP running, a lead-admitted receipt whose helper is killed reaches completed or failed after the lead MCP exits, while the queue run is alive, with no further RPC (test)
An `applying` receipt is still decided by the commit-marker check and is never applied twice; existing thin-mcp-ticket-commits tests still pass

tickets.title: Ticket edits never starve behind back-to-back lands
tickets.what: 2026-11-26, observed live: ticket-edit receipts te…0c, 0d, 0e, 0f, 10 and 11 (adds for imp-daily-facts, cold-archive, workflow, unattended, chores and a select-send status update) stayed `queued` for over an hour while a chain of lands (f76537…, f50dc…, f0420…, fc0f02…) held the main-checkout lease back to back ("waiting for <flow> (gate step 3)"). An earlier receipt (0b) applied, so the drain works, but it never gets a turn: each land hands the lease to the next waiting land. Queue runs and main then act on stale ticket state (a run started before a status update dispatched a ticket against the intended dependency, a duplicate repair ticket landed, a ready ticket waited). Give queued ticket edits priority at every lease handoff: when a land releases or hands over the main-checkout lease and edits are pending, drain them (bounded: the pending batch at that moment, each a small commit) before the next land takes the lease. A land that is mid-gate is not interrupted. JSON-store features (ticket-store) are lease-free and unaffected; this covers Markdown features until their migration.

acceptance.text: With two lands chained back to back and an edit queued during the first gate, the edit commits between the two lands (test)
Draining is bounded to the edits pending at the handoff; a steady stream of edits cannot starve lands (test)
A land waiting for the lease after the drain proceeds without a gate rerun caused by the edit commits beyond the usual base-move replay
docs/reference.md states the order: running land, then pending edits, then the next land

tickets.title: One handoff drain per train outcome; reset drain bookkeeping for the single fallback
tickets.what: Repair for mcp-latency/05 (milestone review jeb31e6e4318ab7e2). In `src/mcp/land-runner.ts` `train()`, when a train partially succeeds and the lease-owning helper's own pick is excluded from `members`, `publish(who, tips)` already drains the handoff snapshot (via `drainHandoff()` at ~:463), then `train()` falls through and calls `drainPendingTicketEdits` again (~:567) before the owner's single attempt — two batches at one handoff, so an edit admitted during the first drain commits ahead of the waiting single. In reverse, `handoffDrained` stays true from that partial publish while the single runs under the same lease, so if the single exits via the failure/cancel `finally` (~:609) it skips its own pending batch. Fix: make one handoff decision per train outcome — reuse the drain a successful publish already did, drain exactly once on a clean unpublished fallback (no publish), and reset `handoffDrained = false` when the single attempt starts so its own exit drains. Delete the now-redundant direct second drain call. Keep CustodianError/publish_pending skips as they are.

acceptance.text: A partial train where the lease owner's pick is excluded drains exactly one snapshot before the owner's single attempt; an edit admitted during the train's publish drain does not commit before the single attempt (regression test that forces the lease owner to be the excluded pick)
After a partial train publish, a single attempt that then fails or is cancelled still drains its pending batch before releasing the lease (test)
A train that publishes nothing (clean fallback) drains once before the single attempt, as before
The steady-stream boundedness test synchronizes at least one receipt admission inside the snapshot drain so it deterministically proves post-snapshot arrivals wait for the next turn
npm test, npm run test:mjs and check:fixtures pass
